Tonight's starting five is now inside every number from the moment lineups post. A reserve who starts gets his extra minutes, and a usual starter left out of the five is cut and flagged. On 1,199 of last season's games that the lessons never saw, minutes at tip-off landed 10% closer and points 2.8% closer.

The first quarter was the app's blind spot: 6 to 9 minutes in, it projected minutes worse than at tip-off. Minutes now land 7 to 11% closer there, points about 2% closer, and the final score 4 to 5% closer at 6 minutes in and at the end of Q1 (same 1,199 games).

Between checkpoints the app now blends the lessons of the two nearest stages instead of jumping from one to the next. At 15 minutes in, minutes landed 8% closer and points 1% closer (400 unseen games).
About one player a game who went on to play 10+ minutes had no number at tip-off: deep-bench players on short-handed nights and players back from a layoff. They now get one as soon as lineups post.

Before tip-off each player's number answers 'what if he plays', because a pick on a player who sits is no action. The game score is scaled to the minutes a team can really play, so a long active list no longer inflates it.
From halftime on the gain is small (about 0.3% on points). Before lineups are posted nothing moved: the app only has the injury report then, and that number is still at the limit luck allows.
Lessons now come from 3,586 games across three seasons (1,314 before). Every plus edge shown is saved and graded on this phone: see EDGE RECORD above.
